correctness.rationale: Every binary word has a unique greedy arch decomposition; for each leading a^m opposite(a) the earliest-match criterion proves s_opposite(w)=s(v), and s_a(w)=s_a(v) if m=1 else zero. The resulting two-by-two transfers are exact even for unary/empty rests. The weighted all-arch matrix has the common eigenvector (1,1), yielding H=2/(1-z-u z^2(3-z)). Binomial extraction proves T_{n,k}; setting u=1 proves the recurrence. The cubic has three simple real roots in (-1,-1/2),(0,1/2),(3,4), ensuring unique dominant root and correct residue. Direct independent subsequence enumeration passes all 32767 words through length14, 8166 arch transfers and 64 bivariate coefficient cells; finite checks are corroboration only.

value.rationale: A shortest absent subsequence marks the first failure of scattered-subsequence universality, a standard invariant of words. The all-length, all-index weighted generating function computes the complete exact first moment conditioned on the universality index, rather than ad hoc isolated values. The exponential mean with sharp base 1.085043... is a nontrivial structural counterpart to existing unweighted and maximum-count laws. Although the scalar sequence is tabulated, the bivariate classification, binary SAS interpretation, proof mechanism and joint exact enumeration have independent mathematical explanatory value.
